name: Manny Rutinel

summary.text: Manny Rutinel is a Colorado state representative for House District 32, an attorney, and a former economist for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
An Adams County Democratic vacancy committee appointed him to the Colorado House of Representatives on October 9, 2023, to replace Dafna Michaelson Jenet.

He earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida (2016), a master's degree in economics from Johns Hopkins University (2018), and a J.D. from Yale Law School (2022); he has also worked as chief executive officer of Climate Refarm.

experience.text: Colorado House of Representatives, District 32, since October 9, 2023; serves on the Energy and Environment Committee (2025-2026).
Economist, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; served as a first responder in Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria.
Attorney; chief executive officer of Climate Refarm.

record.title: SB25-003, Semiautomatic Firearms & Rapid-Fire Devices
record.detail: Cosponsor. Prohibits manufacturing, distributing, transferring, selling, or purchasing specified semiautomatic firearms with detachable magazines absent a permit/training exception; became law.

record.title: SB25-129, Legally Protected Health-Care Activity Protections
record.detail: Cosponsor. Allows prescription labels for mifepristone and misoprostol to list only the prescribing practice rather than the practitioner's name, among other protections; became law.

record.title: SB25-276, Protect Civil Rights Immigration Status
record.detail: Cosponsor. Prohibits a jail custodian from delaying a defendant's release for the purpose of an immigration enforcement operation, among other provisions; became law.

record.title: HB24-1134, Adjustments to Tax Expenditures to Reduce Burden
record.detail: Prime sponsor. Expanded the state Earned Income Tax Credit for low-income families.

record.title: SB25-006, Investment Authority of State Treasurer for Affordable Housing
record.detail: Prime sponsor. Created a fund to help finance affordable housing.

positions.source_title: SB25-129 Legally Protected Hlth-Care Activity Protections | Colorado General Assembly
positions.quote: the act authorizes a prescription label for mifepristone, misoprostol, and the generic alternatives to those prescriptions to include only the name of the prescribing health-care practice
positions.note: Cosponsored this law protecting abortion-medication prescribers; reinforced by his campaign site: "When it comes to abortion, the government needs to respect Americans’ freedom to make our own decisions about our own families without interference from politicians."

positions.source_title: SB25-003 Semiautomatic Firearms & Rapid-Fire Devices | Colorado General Assembly
positions.quote: The act prohibits knowingly manufacturing, distributing, transferring, selling, or purchasing a specified semiautomatic firearm on or after August 1, 2026
positions.note: Cosponsor of this 2025 law restricting certain semiautomatic firearms, cited directly in the statement's coding guide.

positions.source_title: SB25-276 Protect Civil Rights Immigration Status | Colorado General Assembly
positions.quote: The act prohibits the jail custodian from delaying a defendant's release for the purpose of an immigration enforcement operation.
positions.note: Cosponsored this law limiting jail cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; his campaign site calls it a bill that "keeps Colorado law enforcement focused on keeping us safe rather than supporting ICE’s cruelty."

positions.quote: We need an immigration enforcement system that improves public safety and national security by focusing on the deportation of violent criminals, gang members, and human traffickers – not our neighbors who contribute to our communities
positions.note: Explicitly supports deporting people convicted of serious crimes while opposing broader deportation and favoring a path to citizenship for long-settled immigrants; coded as an explicit mixed position rather than agree or disagree.

positions.quote: Trump and Gabe Evans’ cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act will kick hundreds of thousands of Coloradans off their health care.
positions.note: Opposes Medicaid/ACA cuts and campaigns on expanding affordability of coverage.

positions.quote: Trump’s tariffs drive up the cost of everyday goods like groceries and housing.
positions.note: Campaign site states he will "stop his tariffs," making opposition to broad tariffs a signature message.

positions.quote: their budget cuts take away earned benefits like Social Security, Medicaid, and Medicare - benefits Trump calls “entitlements” - to pay for massive tax cuts for the wealthy and big corporations
positions.note: Direct criticism of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's tax and spending provisions, a central campaign theme.

research_notes: Finance is federal and left null per protocol, though Ballotpedia notes he had raised $4.34 million as of June 30, 2026, for reference. On his Ballotpedia page, opponent Gabe Evans' Candidate Connection survey states Rutinel 'voted no on mandating minimum prison sentences for people who traffic and buy child sex slaves' in the state legislature, which would bear on the fentanyl-penalties and child-trafficking-life statements; this claim comes from Evans' campaign, not from Rutinel's own words or a verified vote record, so it was not used to code a position for Rutinel, and a reviewer may want to verify the underlying Colorado bill and vote. No direct statement found on energy/climate policy, public lands, or Colorado ballot measures on hunting rights, mail ballot ID, redistricting, or plain-language ballots. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-research; relied on Ballotpedia, his campaign site, and leg.colorado.gov bill pages via direct fetch.
